chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who makes a vow of abstention (ila') from his wife. He said: 'Ila' is when the man says, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period.' Then he waits for four months. If he returns (to intimacy), that is fulfillment (ifa'). And fulfillment is when he reconciles with his family. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return after four months, until he reconciles with his family or is divorced, he will be compelled to do so. And a divorce does not take effect between them until it is confirmed. And if it is after the four months, if he refuses, the Imam separates them.

key_terms.إِيفَاء: Fulfillment (of the vow by returning to intimacy)
key_terms.إِيلَاء: Vow of abstention from sexual intercourse with one's wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for Ila (vow of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the mechanics of Ila', specifying that the four-month waiting period begins upon the vow and that the husband is compelled by the Imam to either resume intimacy or divorce if he persists. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the divorce remains pending (muda') during this period, ensuring the wife's rights are protected before final separation. The text emphasizes divine mercy ('Ghafur Rahim') as the theological basis for this temporary suspension of marital duties.
